findings.what: The stage says the Astana zone is its only behavior change. We measured a second one. In production, a HEAD request that ends in an error page (measured on missing paths; by the source the same holds for the 500 page) gets different headers after this stage: Content-Length goes from the size of the page (1564 for the 404 page) to 0 for every client, and Content-Type goes from 'text/html; charset=UTF-8' to '*/*; charset=UTF-8' for clients that send 'Accept: */*', which is what curl, most uptime monitors and link checkers send. Status codes do not change, GET responses do not change, and HEAD requests to pages that exist do not change. The cause is in Rails: since 7.2.3 the public exceptions application answers HEAD with an empty body in the format the request asked for. The Action Pack 7.2 changelog lists it as 'Always return empty body for HEAD requests in PublicExceptions and DebugExceptions' (https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v7.2.4/actionpack/CHANGELOG.md). No recorded request could show it: the 170 recorded requests run in the test environment, where exceptions are raised and never rendered, and none is a HEAD. The impact is small and no application code is wrong. What has to change is text: declare the difference, sourced, so the count of declared changes is two, and say whether a monitor that reads Content-Type or Content-Length on HEAD needs telling. The author may also want one recorded request that renders an error page, so later hops are compared on this path.
findings.where: exec/stages/S3/notes.md and pr-body.md, 'Declared behavior changes' (source: actionpack 7.2.4 lib/action_dispatch/middleware/public_exceptions.rb:35)

findings.what: Carried from the first two reviews, still open: json is not pinned below 3 in the Gemfile, and the plan put the pin in S2. Active Support 7.2 and 8.0 pass an option that json 3 removed. Today the lock holds json 2.7.1, JSON encoding works on 7.2.4 (probe), and one thing does hold json back for now: rubocop 1.48.1 in the development group requires json ~> 2.3. That protection goes when rubocop is upgraded or when a bundle is installed without the development group and relocked. Belongs to S2's follow-up or to S4 before its relock. The notes list it as a follow-up.

The second review's defect is fixed. The notes and the pull request text no longer declare a secret key change; they describe it as checked with no change, and the spec comment says the same. We confirmed it again and extended it to the branch nobody had run: with a secret key configured, 7.1.6 and 7.2.4 both use that key and write no local secret file. The migration waiter fix and the conservative lock from the first review also hold; we confirmed both independently. Still open, and the notes say so: bin/rails app:update was not run by the author (we ran it in pretend mode, see the break attempts), the client has column names for stored Astana values but no query, and the seventh change under S3 in out/plan.json still asks for the withdrawn declaration.

The stage's diff adds 70 entries to the committed baseline. Five are the stage's new examples. The other 65 are examples that S1 added (session continuity, the scheduled tasks, the two serialized-column specs, the worker and SMTP server specs) and that the committed baseline on S2 did not list. result.json records baseline_examples_added as 0, and the notes do not mention it. The gate itself was not weakened: the check compared 916 examples one by one before and after, and the committed file now agrees with the suite (904 passed, 17 failed). It is a bookkeeping gap between S1, S2 and this stage that a reader of the diff will ask about. One sentence in the notes would answer it. result.json also shows 'attempts' as 2 at the top and 1 in the check.

Carried from the earlier reviews, and now run instead of only read: errors.each with a two-argument block yields an ActiveModel::Error and nil on 7.2.4, so the line copies a nil message onto the route. Active Model has behaved this way since 7.0, so it is the same before and after this stage. Worth a ticket outside the upgrade.

The notes say deprecation warnings that only appear in production mode were not measured. We measured them for the paths we ran: booting in production, 26 requests through the full stack and the three server processes produced 0 Rails deprecation notifications on 7.2.4. One Ruby warning that 7.1.6 printed in production (Rack's notice about the :unprocessable_entity status name, from Action Pack) is gone on 7.2.4.

method.changelogs_not_read: actioncable, actionmailbox, actiontext, activejob and activestorage for 7.2 (53 entries) were not read: config/application.rb requires six railties and none of these five is among them (inventory.json, framework_config). Entry counts exclude the 'No changes' placeholders; 385 of 438 entries read. Entries that apply: the soft deprecation of ActiveRecord::Base.connection (lib/tasks/postal.rake:31, works, prints nothing); the Astana zone (declared); the 7.2.3 secret_key_base entry (checked, no change on this hop, as the notes now say); show_exceptions true/false removed (changed in test.rb); the Rack 3.2 :unprocessable_entity conversion (two render calls, converted by Rails; the Ruby warning 7.1.6 printed for it in production is gone on 7.2.4); the 7.2.3 entry 'Always return empty body for HEAD requests in PublicExceptions and DebugExceptions' (finding 1: it changes two response headers in production and the stage does not declare it); the HAML capture fix (recorded responses identical). We searched repo/ for the removed, renamed and deprecated names in the seven changelogs (connection and pool methods, enum, serialize, alias_attribute, the removed Active Support configuration names, Deprecation class methods, to_default_s, Rails.application.secrets, content security and permissions policy, parameters compared with a hash, tag helpers and others) and found no use. The environment files and config/initializers/new_framework_defaults_7_0.rb set none of the configuration names 7.2 removed (the defaults file has no active line). We searched the installed source of 23 gems that hook into Rails for nine removed or moved names. Hits besides plain uses of the soft-deprecated connection method in sentry-rails, database_cleaner and shoulda-matchers: kaminari-core (four ActiveSupport::Deprecation.warn calls), sprockets-rails (one), dynamic_form (one), nifty-utils (Rails.application.secrets). We read each and ran the two the application could reach: the kaminari previous and next page tags only warn when a params object is passed, and the one paginate call in the application (servers/queue.html.haml:23) passes none; the sprockets-rails call sits behind unknown_asset_fallback, which is false here. The other two are in helpers the application does not call.

upstream_diff.why_not: We read every patch on the two branches. For the open pull request we read its Gemfile, test.rb, schema and migration waiter patches and compared the rest by file list, which is the same as the 8.1.4 branch. None of the 11 files is a break this stage needed. The explicit YAML coder on the two serialized columns is only required under the 7.1 defaults; under load_defaults 7.0 both columns resolve to the YAML coder on 7.2.4 and round trip, with psych 5.4.0 loaded (probe). Replacing dynamic_form is their choice: its helpers work on 7.2.4 and the recorded invalid-form responses match. The framework defaults files are the config stage's work; bin/rails app:update on this branch would create new_framework_defaults_7_2.rb and offers changes to 14 existing files, all optional (break attempt 9). db/schema.rb and the annotate rake files belong to the 8.1 hop and to S2. The two application files both sides change (lib/migration_waiter.rb, config/environments/test.rb) carry the same change as theirs. Their Gemfile pins json below 3 and this branch does not (finding 2). Their work does not mention the HEAD response difference in finding 1 either.
